3: ## Existing application

5: The CLI in `src/cli/` collects run settings and invokes the graph. `src/tradingagents/graph/` coordinates the four analysts, research debate, trader, risk discussion and portfolio manager. Data tools route through `dataflows/`; model clients live in `llm_clients/`. The graph produces a decision and reports. The memory package records prior decisions and reflections.
6: 
7: ## Team design pending

9: After requirement review, record scope, architectural drivers, external and authority boundaries, integration contracts, workflow changes, permissions, verification, observability and change policy here. Identify the deterministic component that constrains each safety-relevant AI output and link its invariant and negative test.
10: 
11: ## FEAT-01 — Options Analyst (specified)
12: 
13: For stock runs, add a fifth parallel analyst to the default selection. Explicit selections take precedence. The proposed selection key is `options` and the proposed state field is `options_report`. The report describes what stock options imply about risk using eligible option-chain evidence. The Market Analyst owns the underlying stock's price and volume analysis.
14: 
15: | Boundary | Producer and consumer contract |
16: | --- | --- |
17: | Data access | The data layer receives the stock and analysis cutoff and filters records before model invocation. The model interprets eligible records. The application controls eligibility and the unavailable status. |
18: | First-stage state | The analyst publishes one options report or an explicit unavailable notice. A deselected analyst issues no lookup or report. Older explicit selections and saved outputs without this field remain readable. |
19: | Raw evidence | Both researchers and all three risk debaters receive the report, including its unavailable status. |
20: | Derived evidence | Research Manager reads the debate. Trader reads the investment plan and retains the separate technical market report for price levels. Portfolio Manager reads the risk debate, research plan and trade proposal. A rating change is not required. |
21: | Presentation and storage | CLI progress and report panels, graph state and saved run logs expose the selected analyst's result. The shared report writer emits a separate Markdown file and a section in the combined Markdown and requested HTML output. |
22: 
23: The scope decision is recorded in [ADR 001](docs/architecture/adr/001-architecture-choice.md). The [trace matrix](docs/architecture/trace-matrix.md) links each contract to its planned verification.
24: 
25: ## FEAT-02 — Research debate early stop
26: 
27: The bull and bear researchers already alternate turns. Extend the routing decision in
28: `src/tradingagents/graph/conditional_logic.py` at the end of a bull–bear pair. The research
29: debate history is the reference for identifying evidence already cited and opposing arguments
30: already answered. A paraphrase of the same fact or rebuttal adds no progress.
31: 
32: | Decision point | Next step |
33: | --- | --- |
34: | Only the bull has spoken in this round | Give the bear its turn. |
35: | Both have spoken and the round limit is reached | Hand the history to the Research Manager under the existing limit. |
36: | Opening round complete and below the limit | Start round two. |
37: | Later round complete and below the limit | Continue if either side cited a new fact or first addressed an unanswered opposing point. Otherwise record “No new evidence or first response in this round” with the debate and hand the full history to the Research Manager. |
38: 
39: The rule operates on the research debate regardless of which analysts supplied reports. The separate risk debate uses its existing routing.
40: 
41: ## FEAT-03 — Company background in the consolidated report
42: 
43: The shared CLI and Python export path prepares one factual introduction from the run's eligible company profile. Both renderers place it between the report header and the analyst reports. Reuse the ticker in the title. The introduction is independent of the Fundamentals Analyst and requires no additional agent or model call.
44: 
45: A run retains its cleaned profile once at initialization: `create_run_state` resolves the instrument identity a single time and keeps only `company_name`, `industry` and `business_description` in the optional state field `company_identity` (declared `NotRequired`, so a run without it stays loadable). A custom `resolve_instrument_context` override still supplies the run's context string; the profile is retained from that same single resolution, and a failed resolution is not retried, so no extra vendor request is made. That field flows through the graph and is persisted in the run log. The exporter reads only stored run data — no lookup, cache access, prompt-text parsing or model call — prepares the background once in `write_report_tree`, and shares the same raw source text between Markdown and the requested HTML. Each renderer escapes for its own format: Markdown escapes Markdown-significant characters so the source text shows literally, and HTML escapes for HTML, so both formats show the same visible text. An independent `Company Background` section (English labels `Name`, `Industry`, `Business`) sits after the header and before the numbered analyst sections; the HTML contents list names it first. The business description keeps one or two complete source sentences split at sentence boundaries, with no character cap.
46: 
47: For historical runs, follow the identity rule in `src/tradingagents/agents/context.py`. A current name may identify the company if explicitly labelled as current. Present industry and business details as historical facts only when supported for the analysis date. Omit missing fields and show an unavailable notice if the profile supplies none.

2: 
3: **Scope decision, 22 November 2026.** The team lead chose a fifth first-stage role with its own report, confirmed default inclusion and accepted continuing with an unavailable notice when eligible data is missing. Implementation and test approval are pending.
4: 
5: We traced the baseline from analyst registration to the model inputs and report writer. Two researchers and three risk debaters consume the full report set. The trader consumes a separate technical report for price levels. A separate options node fits the first pattern while preserving the latter contract. [Candidate comparison](../evaluation-table.md).

Reinsert the role, cutoff and missing-data rule after compaction. Downstream nodes receive the resulting report. 1: # ADR 002 — Account for token usage in the run statistics handler
2: 
3: Status: Implemented for the CLI. Browser integration awaits FEAT-06.
4: 
5: FR-TOK-01 counts both provider-reported token fields at model completion, across the existing graph and model callback chain. Missing usage contributes nothing. Each run owns one handler. The existing lock guards both accumulation and the first crossing when the total is strictly greater than the threshold. At that point the handler stores one immutable `TokenWarning(total_tokens, threshold)` and invokes its optional receiver outside the lock. Repainting the snapshot does not emit another event. A receiver failure is logged and leaves analysis and the snapshot available.
6: 
7: Read `token_warning_threshold` from run configuration. It defaults to 100000 and can be set with `TRADINGAGENTS_TOKEN_WARNING_THRESHOLD`. An unset or empty setting uses the default. Other values must parse as positive integers, or configuration raises an error naming the setting. The threshold is informational. It does not change the model output limit or checkpoint identity.
8: 
9: The CLI displays the snapshot in the live layout and requests a refresh at the crossing so a short final stage can still show the warning. A terminal without live display support receives one printed warning. The CLI restores temporary message and report logging methods when the run exits.
10: 
11: For FEAT-06, construct a fresh `StatsCallbackHandler(warning_threshold=threshold, on_token_warning=receiver)` per browser analysis. Pass it to the existing model and graph callback paths. The receiver runs on the model-completion thread, so it should enqueue the two values for the current run's activity stream and let the browser layer publish them. The page should read existing counters through `get_stats()` and associate the warning with the current run. Replay TOK-T1 and TOK-T2 through the browser once wired.
12: 
13: We kept the comparison in the callback because it already owns token counts and receives model completion events. Polling the graph stream alone could delay notification during a slow model call. A separate budget controller would duplicate accounting and add an execution policy outside FR-TOK-01.
```

3: This is a leaf module: it imports only ``pydantic`` and the shared structured

7: FR-DEB-01 says the debate ends early when neither side introduces evidence new
8: to this debate nor gives a first substantive reply to a previously unanswered
9: opposing argument. Surface heuristics (new numbers, entities, reply markers) are

11: The judgement is computed once per eligible completed pair, in the bear node.

45:         "this history."
46:     )
47:     confidence: Literal["low", "medium", "high"] = Field(

49:     )

70: def classify_judgement(payload) -> str:

78:         return UNKNOWN
79:

5: class ConditionalLogic:
6:     """Handles conditional logic for determining graph flow."""
7: 
8:     def __init__(self, max_debate_rounds=1, max_risk_discuss_rounds=1):
9:         """Initialize with configuration parameters."""
10:         self.max_debate_rounds = max_debate_rounds
11:         self.max_risk_discuss_rounds = max_risk_discuss_rounds
12: 
13:     def should_continue_debate(self, state: AgentState) -> str:
14:         """Determine if debate should continue.
15: 
16:         The round cap is checked first and always wins. The opening round always
17:         lets both researchers speak. From round two, a completed pair whose
18:         persisted judgement (written by the bear node) is NO_PROGRESS for this
19:         round ends the debate; the router never re-judges.
20:         """
21:         debate = state["investment_debate_state"]
22:         count = debate["count"]
23: 
24:         # Cap takes priority over any progress verdict.
25:         if count >= 2 * self.max_debate_rounds:
26:             return "Research Manager"
27: 
28:         bull_spoke = debate.get("current_response", "").startswith("Bull")
29: 
30:         # An incomplete round gives the other side its turn (order preserved).
31:         if count % 2 != 0:
32:             return "Bear Researcher" if bull_spoke else "Bull Researcher"
33:         if bull_spoke:
34:             return "Bear Researcher"
35: 
36:         # Completed pair: stop only on a confirmed NO_PROGRESS for this round.
37:         if (
38:             debate.get("progress_outcome") == NO_PROGRESS
39:             and debate.get("progress_round") == count // 2
40:         ):
41:             return "Research Manager"
42: 
43:         return "Bull Researcher"
44: 
45:     def should_continue_risk_analysis(self, state: AgentState) -> str:
46:         """Determine if risk analysis should continue."""
47:         if (

49:         ):  # max_risk_discuss_rounds turns each for the three risk analysts
50:             return "Portfolio Manager"
51:         if state["risk_debate_state"]["latest_speaker"].startswith("Aggressive"):
52:             return "Conservative Analyst"
53:         if state["risk_debate_state"]["latest_speaker"].startswith("Conservative"):
54:             return "Neutral Analyst"
55:         return "Aggressive Analyst"

16: def _imports(path: Path) -> set[str]:
17:     names = set()

# FEAT-05 plan — Paragraph citations in the research debate (FR-CIT-01)

Baseline inspected at `HEAD = a99c19b` (`docs(FEAT-04): record token warning design and verification`). Working tree already has one unrelated modification (`docs/ai-use-log.yaml`) and an untracked `opencode.json`; both were left untouched.

## 1. Completion criteria and requirement → test mapping

**Criteria** (all must hold before handoff):
1. The text both researchers receive numbers only the *body* paragraphs of each supplied report, with a stable prefix per source and a two-digit sequence from `01`; the original paragraph text is unchanged.
2. Each bull/bear turn records, beside that turn, the IDs the model gave; unknown IDs are marked invalid and turns with none are marked uncited; the debate still continues in both cases.
3. Source paragraph labels appear on the source paragraphs and the citation/validation annotations appear beside the arguments in individual files, consolidated Markdown **and** the requested HTML.
4. IDs are identical across the two researchers, unchanged when a report is processed twice (streaming chunks, export), and stable across a checkpoint resume.
5. Old state/logs without the new fields still load, route, export and display; CLI, public imports and graph routing are unchanged.
6. Evidence recorded: full offline suite, targeted suites, `ruff`, requirements-schema check.

| FR-CIT-01 (compatibility: Options reports and FEAT-02) | §4, §6 | AGENTS.md preservation rule | **CIT-T5**, **CIT-T3**, **CIT-T6 (new, proposed)** |

All CIT cases remain **proposed**; none are approved and none have been executed.

## 2. Editable / frozen paths and affected interfaces

**Proposed editable (implementation round)**
- `src/tradingagents/agents/citations.py` — **new leaf module**, single owner of numbering, labelling, validation, annotation and the rendered debate text.
- `src/tradingagents/agents/researchers/bull_researcher.py`, `bear_researcher.py` — prompt sources + returned state.

- Authority split: the **program** assigns IDs, renders labelled sources, resolves citations and writes the fixed notices (authoritative). The **model** supplies only the IDs it cites (advisory input that is never trusted). This is the deterministic component constraining the AI output; negative cases CIT-T2/CIT-T5 are the violation tests.

## 3. Numbering, arguments, validation, state ownership, export flow

**3.1 Paragraph numbering.** Blank-line–separated blocks; skip empty blocks, headings (`#`–`######`), fenced code blocks and table lines. Every other block receives the next ID. Original text is kept verbatim, including multi-line blocks (lists) and a plain-text fallback for heading-only/empty reports. Prefixes: `MKT` market, `SEN` sentiment, `NWS` news, `FUN` fundamentals, `OPT` options (aligned with OPT-T4's existing `1_analysts/options.md`/`OPT` naming). Two digits, overflow-safe (`-100` after `-99`). Unselected/absent reports get no IDs.

**3.2 Argument boundaries.** One researcher turn = one `llm.invoke`. The argument body is the model's returned text minus its citation labels; the labels beside the argument are the **union** of IDs (a) written in that turn and (b) present in the run's state, so IDs survive repeated processing and a replay. The numbered numbering is computed from report text only — never from prompts, history or export — so it cannot drift.

**3.3 Citation validation.** Each extracted ID is matched against `report_paragraphs` for this run. Unknown → kept as written and marked `Invalid citation`; none → argument marked `No citation provided`. Marks are deterministic strings written by the program, never requested from the model (a model-authored "invalid" label would be an unverified claim). The debate continues because `should_continue_debate` and the judge are untouched.

**3.4 State ownership.** `report_paragraphs` is written once when the handoff rows are first built (from the analysts' reports, which therefore cannot change afterwards); the bull and bear both read that single stored mapping. `turn_citations`/`citation_notes` are appended by each researcher node, carried by the manager, logged by `_log_state`, and only rendered by the exporters. All three are optional, so a state or log without them still routes, exports and displays.

**3.5 Markdown/HTML flow.** `reporting.py` renders the labelled source paragraphs for section I and the annotated debate for section II once, and passes the same prepared text through `parts` to `report_html.py` (which already parses agent text as CommonMark with raw HTML off and escapes its own labels). Inline code labels render identically in both formats; the HTML CSP and escaping are unchanged. Annotations are appended after the argument so the source paragraph content itself is never altered.

## 4. Stable IDs: both researchers, repeated processing, resume

- **Both researchers** consume the same `report_paragraphs` mapping, so their labels cannot disagree (CIT-T4).
- **Repeated processing**: numbering is a pure function of report text; a second `stream_run` chunk, a second `write_report_tree` call or a second node invocation on the same state yields identical IDs and identical annotations. Only `save_reports`/`write_report_tree` write files (the CLI's intermediate `message_tool.log`/report-section logger is left as a raw activity log).
- **Resume**: the mapping lives in graph state, which a checkpoint commits, and it is derived from report text, so a resumed run re-derives the same IDs; no new config key is added to `_run_signature`.

## 5. Positive and negative tests

**CIT-T1 (positive, proposed).** Fixed fundamentals report with a heading and two distinct body paragraphs separated by a blank line; bull cites the first, bearer the second; repeated with an options report added. Expect `FUN-01`/`FUN-02` on the same original paragraphs in both runs, no ID on the heading, `OPT-01` first in options; each export has one matching labelled source paragraph per citation and the IDs beside the right arguments.

**CIT-T2 (negative, proposed).** One claim citing two valid paragraphs, one citing absent `FUN-99`, one with no citation. Valid IDs stay beside the first claim; `Invalid citation` and `No citation provided` appear in Markdown and HTML; the debate reaches the Research Manager.

**CIT-T3 (proposed, FEAT-02 interaction).** Below the cap, the bearer answers an outstanding bull point using the bull's same valid ID; both resolve to that paragraph and a scripted FEAT-02 `PROGRESS` judgement continues the debate (the judge prompt/history is not changed by FEAT-05).

**CIT-T4 (new, proposed).** Both researcher prompts contain identical labels for each supplied report; a repeated `stream_run` chunk and a second export reproduce identical IDs; a checkpoint resume yields the same IDs and a full debate history.

**CIT-T5 (new, proposed, Options).** Options-only run: `OPT-01`… numbering, an options-cited argument annotated correctly, and the Options Analyst prompt/evidence path unchanged (FEAT-01 markers still reach both researchers).

**CIT-T6 (new, proposed, compatibility/negative).**
- A FEAT-03-style consolidated export still shows one `Company Background` section after the header, before numbered sections, with no paragraph IDs in it; the debate and decision sections follow. Export does not rewrite `company_identity`.
- Baseline state/log without the new fields still exports and displays, with no crash.
- Full offline graph run (scripted models, no network) still reaches a decision and writes a valid JSON run log.

Every test states its requirement/case ID in its docstring, per `verification-constraints.md`.

## 6. Existing offline regression and structural verification commands

Commands recorded for the verification stage (to be run in a **fresh** environment; see the environment note):

## 7. Open decisions, tradeoffs, recommended choices

All of the following need your decision; the first is the most consequential.

1. **Where the model's citation label lives (recommended: inline `[FUN-01]` tags + tolerant extraction + program-written annotations).**
   - *Evidence for inline tags*: FEAT-02's reviewer-approved judge text deliberately says "a fact restated with only new citation labels is not new" (`debate_progress.py`), which presupposes labels inside turn text. And both researchers read the same `history` string, so a citation kept only outside the turn would be invisible to the next speaker and to the judge.
   - *Tradeoff*: the FEAT-02 judge prompt is frozen; inline labels add a few tokens and could slightly change the semantics the judge is already unvalidated on. A separate "Citations" block keeps source arguments clean but hides them from the debate.
2. **Approve two new cases (CIT-T4 stability both-researchers/repeat/resume; CIT-T6 Options + FEAT-02/export compatibility + legacy state).** Recommended: yes — FR-CIT-01 is satisfied on Options runs and old states only if these are shown; they fill the fit criterion "inconsistent export" and "interrupted debate".
3. **State fields.** Recommended: three optional debate fields (`report_paragraphs`, `turn_citations`, `citation_notes`) persisted in the run log additively. Rejected alternative: derive from report text at export time only — invisible to the next speaker, the judge and replay.
4. **`_bear_with_judge` helper.** Recommended: **phase 0** probe deciding whether existing FEAT-02 tests still pass with the new bear prompt before any test edit; if needed, edit the helper only, with explicit approval and no assertion weakened (FEAT-02 precedent). 5. **Prefix and annotation wording.** Recommended: `MKT/SEN/NWS/FUN/OPT` and exactly `Invalid citation` / `No citation provided`; alternatives: longer prefixes (`FUND`) or bracketed marks. Prefixes are cheap to change now and expensive after tests are approved.
6. **Which arguments get scanned** (recommended): researcher turns only; the Research Manager plan, trader and risk debate are not citation targets in this scope.
7. **CLI display.** Recommended: reuse the same rendered debate text in `display_complete_report` for consistency; the FEAT-06 activity view is out of scope and will consume the same prepared text later.
8. **Proposed doc updates** (carry into the implementation/handoff round, not this plan): trace-matrix FEAT-05 evidence, `runtime-policy-catalog.md` rows for invalid/uncited citations (deterministic response + negative test), review memo row, AI-use log entry, and the proposed permission-model allowlist below.
9. **Permission allowlist (proposed, awaiting team approval).**
   *Coding agent*: write only the editable paths above; no other test edits; no `.opencode/rules.md`; no requirements/design text for approved features; no network.
   *`citations`/handoff component*: read `market_report`, `sentiment_report`, `news_report`, `fundamentals_report`, `options_report`; write `report_paragraphs`, `turn_citations`, `citation_notes`.
   *Researcher nodes*: read the stored mapping and own history; write only their own turn and the citation fields.
   *Exporter*: read-only over run state; writes only the report tree files it already owns.
   *CLI display*: read-only.
10. **Known environment defect** (item in §6): the stale installed `tradingagents` must not be used for FEAT-05 evidence; recommended fix is a clean editable install in a fresh environment, recorded as an intervention.

**Not claimed:** no approval of this plan or of any test; no test passing for FEAT-05; FEAT-02 semantic accuracy remains unverified as recorded.

Added — debate-state keys `report_paragraphs`, `turn_citations`, `citation_notes` (all optional); additive `_log_state` keys; `cli.display._md_inline` (additive helper).
Authority: the **program** assigns IDs, segments arguments, validates and writes notices (authoritative). The **model** writes only the labels it cites (advisory, never trusted). Negative cases CIT-T2/CIT-T4 are the violation tests for that split.

## 3. Numbering, arguments, validation, history, exports

**3.1 Paragraph map — first stored and reused.** The map (`{FUN-01: "Revenue grew 10%…", FUN-02: "Valuation is 40x…"}`, plus the ordered source list) is stored in `investment_debate_state["report_paragraphs"]` **once, by the first researcher node that runs** (always the Bull, the graph's entry into the debate), built from the analysts' reports at that moment. Both researchers, both exports and the run log read that stored map; nothing rebuilds it from reports, prompts or history. Reports cannot change after the analysts finish, so the map cannot drift. Consequence for resume: see §4.

**3.2 Paragraph numbering (what is numbered)**
- Input is the report split into blank-line–separated blocks. Numbered: blocks whose first line is prose, a list item, a block quote or a table.
- **Not numbered, by design:**
  - Heading-only blocks (`#`–`######`, including the body text that may follow a heading immediately — see §3.6): a heading names a section, not a claim; numbering it would make every citation able to point at a label rather than evidence, and the blueprint says "skip headings".
  - Fenced code blocks: content is literal machine text (numbers, tickers, commands) copied verbatim; it is not analysis prose and its blank lines/symbols would split or merge blocks unpredictably.
  - Table header/delimiter/row blocks: a table is one evidence unit whose rows have no stable prose identity (a re-ordered or re-wrapped row would silently change what an ID means); a summary table's ID points to the whole table instead.
- Every *other* block gets the next ID in source order, two digits (`FUN-01`…`FUN-99`, then `-100`). Prefixes `MKT/SEN/NWS/FUN/OPT` (matches OPT-T4's existing `OPT` naming). Text is preserved verbatim, multi-line list items included. An unselected report gets no IDs.

**3.3 Arguments inside a turn, and citation extraction**
- Segmentation: the model's turn text is split into **arguments** — one per Markdown block (prose paragraph, list item, block quote, table caption/line) using the same block splitter as §3.2; fenced code inside a turn is attached to the preceding argument and not itself an argument; a heading inside a turn starts no argument.
- Each argument is recorded with its own text, its own inline labels and their **character positions in that argument**.
- Extraction: labels are read **only from the current argument's text**. The run's map is used **only** to validate them. A label is never added to an argument because the map contains its ID, and never carried from another argument, a previous turn or the history.
- Validation per argument: known IDs stay as written (positions kept); unknown IDs stay as written and the argument is marked `Invalid citation`; an argument with no label is marked `No citation provided`.

**3.4 How notices enter history and the Research Manager input (before export).**
- The bull/bear node writes `turn_citations` = one entry per argument, in order: `{speaker, turn, argument_index, text, citations:[{id, position, valid}], note}`, where `note` is `""`, `Invalid citation` or `No citation provided` — written by the program, never requested from the model.
- The node writes the **recorded turn** into `history`, `bull_history`, `bear_history` and `current_response`: the model's turn text with each `Invalid citation` / `No citation provided` notice appended **in place, at the end of the argument it belongs to**. So the recorded history that the Research Manager receives already carries the notices; export renders the same recorded strings; nothing is added only at export time.
- Exact worked example — one bear turn with three arguments, after the map from §3.1:

```
Bull Analyst: Revenue grew 10% on strong demand [FUN-01].
Bear Analyst: Margins fell 2 points while volume rose [FUN-01]
 — *Invalid citation: FUN-99.* Valuation is stretched at 40x earnings. — *No citation provided.*
Let me take the revenue point first: the 10% came from one large customer, so it is
concentrated risk. — *No citation provided.*
```

  - Argument 1 (`Valuation is stretched at 40x earnings.`) wrote `FUN-99` → history shows it beside *that* argument with `Invalid citation` (the map contains no `FUN-99`; no replacement is invented).
  - Argument 2 (the bare statement after `[FUN-01]` on the first line — see §3.6) carries the `FUN-01` label from its own line and validates; the sentence "Valuation is stretched at 40x earnings." is a **separate** argument with no label → its own `No citation provided`.
  - Argument 3 (the reply) wrote nothing → its own `No citation provided`; it is not marked for argument 2's missing citation.
  - Consolidated Markdown §II and HTML §II render exactly these three arguments with the same three notices; the individual `2_research/bear.md` file contains the same recorded text.
- **FEAT-02 input, unchanged routing:** the judge receives `history` before the current pair plus the current bull/bear turns exactly as the node recorded them — i.e. with notices present but no routing information added. `_render_prompt` continues to say "a fact restated with only new citation labels is not new". Routing is decided only by `should_continue_debate` on `count`/`progress_*`; FEAT-05 writes none of those keys, so cap-first and opening-round behavior are untouched. Whether the judge still labels a notice-bearing turn correctly is a *content* risk to be observed (CIT-T3 uses a scripted judgement; no semantic claim is made — FEAT-02 semantic accuracy remains unverified).

**3.5 Markdown/HTML flow.** `reporting.py` renders the recorded debate (already notice-bearing) once and passes it to `report_html.py` through `parts`; the HTML keeps raw HTML off and its CSP. Source labels (`[FUN-01]`) are Markdown-rendered, which keeps a single-line list item intact in both formats; the CLI display uses the same rendered text. Annotations never alter the source paragraph content.

**3.6 Heading immediately followed by body text.** A heading block that owns following prose lines with no blank line is **two blocks**: the heading (unnumbered) and the prose that starts at its first non-heading line (numbered normally). Prose with no heading and prose after a blank line are one numbered block; anything separating them (blank line, heading, code fence, table) starts a new block. This is stated so CIT-T1's "heading has no ID" and "one ID per body paragraph" can both hold.

## 4. Graph layout, repeated processing, resume

- **Graph layout unchanged:** no node, edge, entry point or router change; `DEBATE_PATH_MAP` and `RISK_ANALYSIS_PATH_MAP` untouched (CIT-T9 asserts this).

A second `stream_run` chunk, a second node invocation on the same state or a second export yields identical IDs and notices; annotations are appended to the *turn text* that is stored, so re-rendering cannot double-append (the stored turn already contains them).

Recommended forward-only fix (does not change the graph): each researcher node reuses the stored map **if present**, otherwise builds and returns it (§3.1's "first stored" rule then holds on resume too). This is decision 4c; without it, CIT-T7 covers only resumes at/after the first researcher turn.

## A2. Segmentation — one consistent rule, no contradictions

**Block R (one rule).** A report is split into blank-line–separated blocks, then each block is classified in order:

| Block | Numbered? | Argument in a turn? |
|---|---|---|
| Heading line (`#`–`######`) | No. A heading **in its own block** owns what follows; body text after the next blank line is its own block. | No |
| Body paragraph (prose, including any text directly after a heading line on a following block) | **Yes**, one ID | **Yes**, one argument |
| List item (`-`, `*`, `+`, `1.`), one per item, including nested items | **Yes**, one ID per item | **Yes**, one argument per item |
| Block quote | **Yes**, one ID | **Yes**, one argument |
| Table (header + delimiter + all rows, from the blank line before the first row to the blank line after the last) | **Yes — a whole table receives one ID**, never one per row | **Yes**, one argument |
| Fenced code block (```` ``` ```` or `~~~`) | **No.** Its content is literal machine text, not analysis prose, and it is never numbered or segmented | Attached **in full to the argument that immediately precedes it**; if it opens the turn, it is its own argument and is never cited |

- **Adjacent list items without blank lines**: the list items are **not** one block. The splitter runs a second pass inside any block that starts with a list-item marker: it breaks before **every** list-item marker, and before a deeper-indented continuation that follows an item. So

  ```
  - Margins fell 2 points [FUN-01]
  - Valuation is 40x [FUN-99]
  - Demand is opaque
  ```
  is **three** numbered paragraphs in a report and **three** arguments in a turn, each with its own notice in the §A1 style.
- **Heading immediately followed by body text on the next line** (e.g. `## Risks` then `Margins fell…` with no blank line): the heading is one unnumbered block and the body text is one numbered block; the heading gets no ID and the body text gets the next ID. This is the same result as if a blank line separated them.
- **Body text directly after a list item** without a blank line is part of that list item's block (one argument), never a separate argument.

## A3. §4 resume — the paragraph map is built only when the field is absent

- Each researcher node reads `investment_debate_state["report_paragraphs"]`. **If the key is absent**, the node builds the map from the analysts' reports and returns it. **If the key is present, it is used as-is — including an empty map `{}`**. An empty map is *initialized state* (a run with no supplied reports), not a missing field, so it is never rebuilt; this keeps IDs from appearing mid-run and keeps the map identical on every later turn.
- Storage timing: the map is first stored by the first researcher turn that runs (the Bull in a fresh run; the first researcher turn after the resume point in a resumed run), and from then on only read.
- **Resume covered on both sides of the first researcher turn:**
  - *Before* the first researcher turn (interrupted during or after analysts): resume reaches a bull node with no `report_paragraphs` key → it builds and stores the map → the bear sees the same map. Covered by CIT-T7a.
  - *After* the first researcher turn (interrupted after a bull turn): the checkpoint already holds the map → the bear reuses it, builds nothing. Covered by CIT-T7b.
  - Both cases assert identical IDs for the same reports, `_run_signature` unchanged, and the map present exactly once in the final state/log. No new graph node or edge, and no config key.
- **How stored raw argument text prevents duplicate annotations:** `turn_citations` records each argument's **raw model text** (exactly what the model wrote, no notice) alongside its resolved citations and `note`. Annotations are never stored inside that raw text; the annotated turn is **derived** from it (`render_annotated_turn`) when the history string is built and when export renders. Therefore a second node invocation, a repeated `stream_run` chunk, a re-export or a resume cannot append a second notice: there is only ever one rendered copy per render, and the model's words — including any `[FUN-xx]` it wrote — are never deleted, rewritten or reordered.

1. **Plan approved** (this plan + addendum), then
2. **Test-only patch** (new test files; no source changes), then
3. **Explicit test approval**, then
4. **Implementation** (source only), then
5. **Human review of the diff**, then

The Portfolio Manager, Trader, and Research Manager all follow the same
canonical pattern:

1. At agent creation, wrap the LLM with ``with_structured_output(Schema)``
   so the model returns a typed Pydantic instance. If the provider does

   wrap is skipped and the agent uses free-text generation instead.

   markdown. If the structured call itself fails for any reason

def _graph(tmp_path, monkeypatch, model, debug=False, **config):
    cfg = copy.deepcopy(DEFAULT_CONFIG)
    cfg.update(results_dir=str(tmp_path / "results"), data_cache_dir=str(tmp_path / "cache"),
               memory_log_path=str(tmp_path / "log.md"), **config)
    monkeypatch.setattr(trading_graph, "create_tier_client", lambda config, tier, **k: _Client(model))
    return trading_graph.TradingAgentsGraph(config=cfg, debug=debug)


@pytest.mark.unit
@pytest.mark.parametrize("structured", [False, True], ids=["free-text", "structured"])
def test_a_full_run_reaches_a_logged_decision(tmp_path, monkeypatch, offline, structured):
    graph = _graph(tmp_path, monkeypatch, ScriptedModel(structured=structured))

    state, signal = graph.propagate("NVDA", TRADE_DATE)

    assert signal == state["final_rating"] == "Overweight"
    for key in ("market_report", "sentiment_report", "news_report", "fundamentals_report",
                "options_report", "investment_plan", "trader_investment_plan",
                "final_trade_decision"):
        assert state[key].strip(), key
    tool_methods = {"get_stock_data", "get_indicators", "get_news", "get_global_news",
                    "get_macro_indicators", "get_prediction_markets", "get_fundamentals",
                    "get_balance_sheet", "get_cashflow", "get_income_statement",
                    "get_insider_transactions", "get_option_chain", "ohlcv"}
    assert offline == tool_methods
    assert [e["rating"] for e in graph.memory_log.load_entries()] == ["Overweight"]


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_an_interrupted_run_resumes_from_its_checkpoint(tmp_path, monkeypatch, offline):
    model = ScriptedModel(fail_at=12)            # past the analysts, before the decision
    graph = _graph(tmp_path, monkeypatch, model, checkpoint_enabled=True)
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="provider unavailable"):
        graph.propagate("NVDA", TRADE_DATE)
    calls_before = len(model.calls)

    _, signal = graph.propagate("NVDA", TRADE_DATE)

    assert signal == "Overweight"
    resumed_calls = len(model.calls) - calls_before
    full_run = ScriptedModel()
    _graph(tmp_path / "fresh", monkeypatch, full_run).propagate("NVDA", TRADE_DATE)
    # The resumed run makes only the calls the interrupted one had not completed.
    assert resumed_calls == len(full_run.calls) - (model.fail_at - 1)


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_a_graph_reused_across_runs_keeps_no_run_state(tmp_path, monkeypatch, offline):
    """A backtest reuses one graph over its whole grid; holding every run's full
    state would grow without bound."""
    graph = _graph(tmp_path, monkeypatch, ScriptedModel())
    for trade_date in ("2026-01-08", TRADE_DATE):
        graph.propagate("NVDA", trade_date)

    held = [v for v in vars(graph).values() if isinstance(v, dict) and TRADE_DATE in v]
    assert held == []
    assert len(list(tmp_path.glob("results/NVDA/TradingAgentsStrategy_logs/*.json"))) == 2


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_the_analysts_run_at_the_same_time(tmp_path, monkeypatch, offline):
    model = ScriptedModel()
    graph = _graph(tmp_path, monkeypatch, model)

    assert not [n for n in graph.graph.get_graph().nodes if n.startswith("Msg Clear")]
    graph.propagate("NVDA", TRADE_DATE)

    assert len(model.threads) > 1


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_a_debug_run_prints_the_analysts_work_and_reaches_the_same_decision(tmp_path, monkeypatch, offline, capsys):
    """Debug mode streams the analysts' own graphs, so their tool calls still print."""
    graph = _graph(tmp_path, monkeypatch, ScriptedModel(), debug=True)

    state, signal = graph.propagate("NVDA", TRADE_DATE)

    assert signal == "Overweight"

"""Test checkpoint resume: crash mid-analysis, re-run resumes from last node."""

import tempfile
import unittest
from typing import TypedDict

from langgraph.graph import END, StateGraph

from tradingagents.graph.checkpointer import (
    checkpoint_step,
    clear_checkpoint,
    get_checkpointer,
    thread_id,
)

# Mutable flag to simulate crash on first run
_should_crash = False


class _SimpleState(TypedDict):
    count: int


def _node_a(state: _SimpleState) -> dict:
    return {"count": state["count"] + 1}


def _node_b(state: _SimpleState) -> dict:
    if _should_crash:
        raise RuntimeError("simulated mid-analysis crash")
    return {"count": state["count"] + 10}


def _build_graph() -> StateGraph:
    builder = StateGraph(_SimpleState)
    builder.add_node("analyst", _node_a)
    builder.add_node("trader", _node_b)
    builder.set_entry_point("analyst")
    builder.add_edge("analyst", "trader")
    builder.add_edge("trader", END)
    return builder


class TestCheckpointResume(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmpdir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.ticker = "TEST"
        self.date = "2026-04-20"

    def test_crash_and_resume(self):
        """Crash at 'trader' node, then resume from checkpoint."""
        global _should_crash
        builder = _build_graph()
        tid = thread_id(self.ticker, self.date)
        cfg = {"configurable": {"thread_id": tid}}

        # Run 1: crash at trader node
        _should_crash = True
        with get_checkpointer(self.tmpdir, self.ticker) as saver:
            graph = builder.compile(checkpointer=saver)

"""LangGraph checkpoint support for resumable analysis runs.

Per-ticker SQLite databases so concurrent tickers don't contend.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import sqlite3
from collections.abc import Generator
from contextlib import contextmanager
from pathlib import Path

from langgraph.checkpoint.sqlite import SqliteSaver

from tradingagents.dataflows.symbols import safe_ticker_component


def _db_path(data_dir: str | Path, ticker: str) -> Path:
    """Return the SQLite checkpoint DB path for a ticker."""
    # Reject ticker values that would escape the checkpoints directory.
    safe = safe_ticker_component(ticker).upper()
    p = Path(data_dir) / "checkpoints"
    p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return p / f"{safe}.db"


def thread_id(ticker: str, date: str, signature: str = "") -> str:
    """Deterministic thread ID for a ticker+date pair.

    ``signature`` folds in graph-shape-affecting run choices so a resume under a
    different graph can't reuse this checkpoint (#1089); omitting it keeps the
    legacy ID.
    """
    base = f"{ticker.upper()}:{date}"
    if signature:
        base = f"{base}:{signature}"
    return hashlib.sha256(base.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]



```

# --- helpers ----------------------------------------------------------------


def report_map(exclude=(), **overrides):
    """Every supplied report, numbered in order with the approved prefixes.

    ``exclude`` omits a report (analyst not selected). ``overrides`` replaces a
    report's text. Returns the ordered list of ``{id, source, report_key, text}``
    the contract stores in ``report_paragraphs``.
    """
    paragraphs = []
    texts = {key: f"Report for {key}." for key in PREFIX}
    for key, value in overrides.items():
        texts[key + "_report" if not key.endswith("_report") else key] = value
    for key, prefix in PREFIX.items():
        if key in exclude:
            continue
        token = {"market": "MKT-", "sentiment": "SEN-", "news": "NWS-",
                 "fundamentals": "FUN-", "options": "OPT-"}[key.rsplit("_", 1)[0]]
        for n, paragraph in enumerate(_source_paragraphs(texts[key]), 1):
            paragraphs.append({
                "id": f"{token}{n:02d}",
                "source": prefix,
                "report_key": key,
                "text": paragraph,
            })
    return paragraphs


def _source_paragraphs(text):
    """Approved source segmentation: blank-line boundaries, headings skipped."""
    import re

    paragraphs = []
    for block in re.split(r"\n[ \t]*\n", text or ""):
        if not block.strip():
            continue
        first = block.strip().splitlines()[0]
        if re.fullmatch(r"#{1,6}\s.*", first) and len(block.strip().splitlines()) == 1:
            continue
        paragraphs.append(block)
    return paragraphs

def _offline_vendors(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """The existing offline fixture's setup, called directly for the E2E tests.

    Imported rather than requested so these tests read as what they are: an
    extension of the existing end-to-end pattern, on that pattern's fixtures.
    """
    from offline.test_graph_end_to_end import offline as _fixture

    return _fixture.__wrapped__(monkeypatch, tmp_path)


def _resume_graph(tmp_path, monkeypatch, model, **config):
    """A checkpointed graph on scripted models (the existing E2E pattern)."""
    from offline.test_graph_end_to_end import _Client
    from tradingagents.graph import trading_graph

    cfg = copy.deepcopy(DEFAULT_CONFIG)
    cfg.update(
        results_dir=str(tmp_path / "results"),
        data_cache_dir=str(tmp_path / "cache"),
        memory_log_path=str(tmp_path / "log.md"),
        checkpoint_enabled=True,
        **config,
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(trading_graph, "create_tier_client", lambda config, tier, **k: _Client(model))
    return trading_graph.TradingAgentsGraph(config=cfg)

    assert history.count(INVALID) <= history.count("Bear Analyst:")
    assert history.count(UNCITED) <= history.count("Bear Analyst:")
    assert history.count(INVALID) <= history.count("Bear Analyst:")

def test_cit_t2_annotated_turn_matches_the_approved_text():
    """CIT-T2: the annotated turn keeps every original citation in place and
    appends each notice to its own argument only."""
    from tradingagents.agents.citations import render_annotated_turn, resolve_turn

    entry = resolve_turn("bear", 1, BEAR_TURN, report_map())

    rendered = render_annotated_turn(entry)
    assert rendered == BEAR_ANNOTATED
    for text in (BEAR_ARG_1_TEXT, BEAR_ARG_2_TEXT, BEAR_ARG_3_TEXT):
        assert rendered.count(text) == 1
    assert rendered.count(INVALID) == 1
    assert rendered.count(UNCITED) == 1

[Tool result]: """Test checkpoint resume: crash mid-analysis, re-run resumes from last node."""

import tempfile
import unittest
from typing import TypedDict

from langgraph.graph import END, StateGraph

from tradingagents.graph.checkpointer import (
    checkpoint_step,
    clear_checkpoint,
    get_checkpointer,
    thread_id,
)

# Mutable flag to simulate crash on first run
_should_crash = False


class _SimpleState(TypedDict):
    count: int


def _node_a(state: _SimpleState) -> dict:
    return {"count": state["count"] + 1}


def _node_b(state: _SimpleState) -> dict:
    if _should_crash:
        raise RuntimeError("simulated mid-analysis crash")
    return {"count": state["count"] + 10}


def _build_graph() -> StateGraph:
    builder = StateGraph(_SimpleState)
    builder.add_node("analyst", _node_a)
    builder.add_node("trader", _node_b)
    builder.set_entry_point("analyst")
    builder.add_edge("analyst", "trader")
    builder.add_edge("trader", END)
    return builder


class TestCheckpointResume(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmpdir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.ticker = "TEST"
        self.date = "2026-04-20"

    def test_crash_and_resume(self):
        """Crash at 'trader' node, then resume from checkpoint."""
        global _should_crash
        builder = _build_graph()
        tid = thread_id(self.ticker, self.date)
        cfg = {"configurable": {"thread_id": tid}}

        # Run 1: crash at trader node
        _should_crash = True
        with get_checkpointer(self.tmpdir, self.ticker) as saver:
            graph = builder.compile(checkpointer=saver)

[Tool result]: """LangGraph checkpoint support for resumable analysis runs.

Per-ticker SQLite databases so concurrent tickers don't contend.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import sqlite3
from collections.abc import Generator
from contextlib import contextmanager
from pathlib import Path

from langgraph.checkpoint.sqlite import SqliteSaver

from tradingagents.dataflows.symbols import safe_ticker_component


def _db_path(data_dir: str | Path, ticker: str) -> Path:
    """Return the SQLite checkpoint DB path for a ticker."""
    # Reject ticker values that would escape the checkpoints directory.
    safe = safe_ticker_component(ticker).upper()
    p = Path(data_dir) / "checkpoints"
    p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return p / f"{safe}.db"


def thread_id(ticker: str, date: str, signature: str = "") -> str:
    """Deterministic thread ID for a ticker+date pair.

    ``signature`` folds in graph-shape-affecting run choices so a resume under a
    different graph can't reuse this checkpoint (#1089); omitting it keeps the
    legacy ID.
    """
    base = f"{ticker.upper()}:{date}"
    if signature:
        base = f"{base}:{signature}"
    return hashlib.sha256(base.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]

def report_map(exclude=(), **overrides):
    """Every supplied report, numbered in order with the approved prefixes.

    ``exclude`` omits a report (analyst not selected). ``overrides`` replaces a
    report's text. Returns the ordered list of ``{id, source, report_key, text}``
    the contract stores in ``report_paragraphs``.
    """
    paragraphs = []
    texts = {key: f"Report for {key}." for key in PREFIX}
    for key, value in overrides.items():
        texts[key + "_report" if not key.endswith("_report") else key] = value
    for key, prefix in PREFIX.items():
        if key in exclude:
            continue
        token = {"market": "MKT-", "sentiment": "SEN-", "news": "NWS-",
                 "fundamentals": "FUN-", "options": "OPT-"}[key.rsplit("_", 1)[0]]
        for n, paragraph in enumerate(_source_paragraphs(texts[key]), 1):
            paragraphs.append({
                "id": f"{token}{n:02d}",
                "source": prefix,
                "report_key": key,
                "text": paragraph,
            })
    return paragraphs


def _source_paragraphs(text):
    """Approved source segmentation: blank-line boundaries, headings skipped."""
    import re

    paragraphs = []
    for block in re.split(r"\n[ \t]*\n", text or ""):
        if not block.strip():
            continue
        first = block.strip().splitlines()[0]
        if re.fullmatch(r"#{1,6}\s.*", first) and len(block.strip().splitlines()) == 1:
            continue
        paragraphs.append(block)
    return paragraphs


def _state(paragraphs=None, debate=None, **extra):

Leverage the provided research and data to highlight potential downsides and counter bullish arguments effectively.

Key points to focus on:

- Risks and Challenges: Highlight factors like market saturation, financial instability, or macroeconomic threats that could hinder the stock's performance.
- Competitive Weaknesses: Emphasize vulnerabilities such as weaker market positioning, declining innovation, or threats from competitors.
- Negative Indicators: Use evidence from financial data, market trends, or recent adverse news to support your position.
- Bull Counterpoints: Critically analyze the bull argument with specific data and sound reasoning, exposing weaknesses or over-optimistic assumptions.
- Engagement: Present your argument in a conversational style, directly engaging with the bull analyst's points and debating effectively rather than simply listing facts.

Resources available:

{instrument_context}
Market research report: {market_research_report}
Social media sentiment report: {sentiment_report}
Latest world affairs news: {news_report}
{fundamentals_label}: {fundamentals_report}
Options market report: {options_report}
Conversation history of the debate: {history}
Last bull argument: {current_response}
Use this information to deliver a compelling bear argument, refute the bull's claims, and engage in a dynamic debate that demonstrates the risks and weaknesses of investing in the {target_label}.
""" + get_language_instruction()

        response = llm.invoke(prompt)

        argument = f"Bear Analyst: {response.content}"

        new_history = history + "\n" + argument
        new_count = investment_debate_state["count"] + 1
        new_investment_debate_state = {
            "history": new_history,
            "bear_history": bear_history + "\n" + argument,
            "bull_history": investment_debate_state.get("bull_history", ""),
            "current_response": argument,
            "count": new_count,
            # Carry any earlier decision forward; a fresh judgement may replace it.
            "progress_outcome": investment_debate_state.get("progress_outcome", ""),
            "progress_round": investment_debate_state.get("progress_round", 0),
            "progress_reason": investment_debate_state.get("progress_reason", ""),
        }

        # FEAT-02: judge only a completed pair between round two and the cap, i.e.
        # an even new count with 4 <= count < 2*cap. The cap and the opening pair
        # never invoke the judge.
        if judge is not None and _is_eligible_pair(new_count):
            round_number = new_count // 2
            previous_bull = investment_debate_state.get("bull_history", "")
            bull_turn = _latest_bull_turn(previous_bull)
            result = evaluate_pair(judge, history, bull_turn, argument, round_number)
            new_investment_debate_state["progress_outcome"] = result.outcome
            new_investment_debate_state["progress_round"] = result.evaluated_round
            new_investment_debate_state["progress_reason"] = (
                EARLY_STOP_REASON if result.outcome == NO_PROGRESS else ""
            )

        return {"investment_debate_state": new_investment_debate_state}

    return bear_node


def _is_eligible_pair(new_count: int) -> bool:
    """A completed pair that sits between round two and the configured cap."""
    if new_count % 2 != 0:
        return False
    cap = int(get_config().get("max_debate_rounds", 1))
    return 4 <= new_count < 2 * cap


def _latest_bull_turn(bull_history: str) -> str:
    """The most recent bull turn from the accumulated bull history."""
    lines = [line for line in (bull_history or "").splitlines() if line.strip()]
    return lines[-1] if lines else ""

{instrument_context}

---

**Rating Scale** (use exactly one):
- **Buy**: Strong conviction in the bull thesis; recommend taking or growing the position
- **Overweight**: Constructive view; recommend gradually increasing exposure
- **Hold**: Balanced view; recommend maintaining the current position
- **Underweight**: Cautious view; recommend trimming exposure
- **Sell**: Strong conviction in the bear thesis; recommend exiting or avoiding the position

The debate always contains conflicting arguments; deciding which side is stronger is the job, so conflict alone is not a reason to Hold. Commit to the side with the stronger case, sized by how decisively it wins. Choose Hold only when the evidence is still balanced after that weighing, or too thin to support a call; do not manufacture a direction to appear decisive. Weigh the bull and bear cases on their merits, independent of which side spoke first or last.

---

**Debate History:**
{history}

## Output

Write these sections, in this order, starting with the recommendation on its own line:

- **Recommendation**: exactly one of Buy / Overweight / Hold / Underweight / Sell
- **Rationale**: which arguments decided it
- **Strategic Actions**: concrete steps for the trader, sized against a standard allocation

{NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS}""" + get_language_instruction()

            "bull_history": investment_debate_state.get("bull_history", ""),

            "progress_round": investment_debate_state.get("progress_round", 0),
            "progress_reason": investment_debate_state.get("progress_reason", ""),
        }

"""


def _markdown() -> MarkdownIt:
    md = MarkdownIt("commonmark", {"html": False}).enable("table").disable("image")
    md.add_render_rule("table_open", lambda *a: '<div class="table"><table>\n')
    md.add_render_rule("table_close", lambda *a: "</table></div>\n")
    return md


def _render_agent_text(md: MarkdownIt, text: str) -> str:
    """An agent's text, its own headings placed below the agent's heading (h3)."""
    tokens = md.parse(text)
    for token in tokens:
        if token.type in ("heading_open", "heading_close"):
            token.tag = f"h{min(int(token.tag[1]) + 3, 6)}"
    return md.renderer.render(tokens, md.options, {})


# What each data category serves, as a reader would name it.
_CATEGORY = {
    "core_stock_apis": "Prices", "technical_indicators": "Indicators", "fundamental_data": "Fundamentals",
    "news_data": "News", "macro_data": "Macro", "prediction_markets": "Prediction markets",
    "options_data": "Options",
}


def _fields(values) -> str:
    return " ".join(f'<span class="field">{escape(str(v))}</span>' for v in values)


def _chain(vendors: str) -> str:
    """A vendor chain in the order it is tried: ``a,b`` reads a, then b."""
    names = [v.strip() for v in str(vendors).split(",") if v.strip()]
    return ' <span class="then">\u2192</span> '.join(_fields([n]) for n in names)


def _group(name: str, values_html: str) -> str:
    return f'<span class="group"><span class="name">{escape(name)}</span>{values_html}</span>'


def _run_details(final_state: dict, settings: dict | None) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """The run details as (label, value HTML); every value from the run is escaped."""
    details = [("Generated", escape(datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")))]
    if settings:
        s = settings.get
        for tier in ("deep", "quick"):
            provider = s(f"{tier}_think_provider") or s("llm_provider", "?")
            details.append((f"{tier.capitalize()} model", _fields([provider, s(f"{tier}_think_llm", "?")])))
        details.append(("Analysts", _fields(analyst_names(s("analysts")))))
        details.append(("Debate rounds", " ".join((
            _group("research", _fields([s("max_debate_rounds", "?")])),
            _group("risk", _fields([s("max_risk_discuss_rounds", "?")])),
        ))))
        vendors = {**(s("data_vendors") or {}), **(s("tool_vendors") or {})}
        if vendors:
            details.append(("Data vendors", " ".join(
                _group(_CATEGORY.get(k, k), _chain(v)) for k, v in vendors.items()
            )))
        details.append(("Version", escape(f"TradingAgents {s('version', '?')}")))
    if final_state.get("memory_note"):
        details.append(("Memory log", escape(final_state["memory_note"])))
    return details


def _company_background_html(background: dict | None) -> str:
    """The Company Background section for a prepared profile view, or ''.

    ``background`` is the shared view ``write_report_tree`` prepared once for
    both formats. Empty/None renders nothing extra, so direct callers keep the
    page they had. Values are escaped; the section precedes the numbered ones.
    """
    if not background:
        return ""
    lines = []
    if background.get("name"):
        suffix = " (current name)" if background.get("name_is_current") else ""
        lines.append(f"<li><strong>Name</strong>: {escape(background['name'])}{escape(suffix)}</li>")
    if background.get("industry"):
        lines.append(f"<li><strong>Industry</strong>: {escape(background['industry'])}</li>")
    if background.get("business_description"):
        lines.append(f"<li><strong>Business</strong>: {escape(background['business_description'])}</li>")
    if lines:
        body = "<ul>" + "".join(lines) + "</ul>"
    else:
        body = ("<p>No company background is available for this run: no company "
                "name, industry or business description was retained.</p>")
    return f'<section id="company-background"><h2>Company Background</h2>\n{body}</section>'


def render_report(ticker: str, final_state: dict, settings: dict | None, parts,
                  *, background: dict | None = None) -> str:
    """The report page: title and rating, what produced the run, contents, sections.

    ``background`` is the Company Background view prepared once by
    ``write_report_tree`` and shared with the Markdown report; when omitted the
    page is rendered without it, unchanged for direct callers.
    """
    md = _markdown()
    rating = run_rating(final_state) if final_state.get("final_trade_decision") else ""
    tone = _TONE.get(rating, "review")
    date = final_state.get("trade_date", "")

    title = f'<span class="ticker">{escape(ticker)}</span>'
    if rating:
        title += f' <span class="rating {tone}">{escape(rating)}</span>'
    details = "".join(
        f'<div class="{"note" if label == "Memory log" else "detail"}">'
        f"<dt>{escape(label)}</dt><dd>{value}</dd></div>"
        for label, value in _run_details(final_state, settings)
    )

"""The whole graph, end to end, with scripted models and no network.

Every tool-using analyst calls each of its tools once through the vendor router,
the debates and managers run, and the decision is parsed and logged. This pins
the wiring: a restructure that drops a node, a tool or an edge fails here.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import copy
import time

import pandas as pd
import pytest
from langchain_core.language_models.chat_models import BaseChatModel
from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, HumanMessage, ToolMessage
from langchain_core.outputs import ChatGeneration, ChatResult
from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableLambda
from pydantic import Field

from tradingagents.agents import context, schemas
from tradingagents.agents.analysts import sentiment_analyst
from tradingagents.dataflows import router
from tradingagents.dataflows.vendors.yahoo import market as yahoo_market, snapshot
from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG
from tradingagents.graph import trading_graph

TRADE_DATE = "2026-01-09"

# Enough for every free-text reader: the PM's labelled rating and the trader's
# closing proposal line.
TEXT = "Report.\n\n**Rating**: Overweight\n\nFINAL TRANSACTION PROPOSAL: **BUY**"

STRUCTURED = {
    schemas.ResearchPlan: schemas.ResearchPlan(
        recommendation=schemas.PortfolioRating.OVERWEIGHT, rationale="r", strategic_actions="a"),
    schemas.TraderProposal: schemas.TraderProposal(action=schemas.TraderAction.BUY, reasoning="r"),
    # The thesis quotes another party's rating; the decision is still the PM's own.
    schemas.PortfolioDecision: schemas.PortfolioDecision(
        rating=schemas.PortfolioRating.OVERWEIGHT, executive_summary="s",
        investment_thesis="Street consensus rating: Buy (28 of 35 analysts)."),
    schemas.SentimentReport: schemas.SentimentReport(
        overall_band=schemas.SentimentBand.NEUTRAL, overall_score=5.0, confidence="low", narrative="n"),
}

ARGS = {"symbol": "NVDA", "ticker": "NVDA", "curr_date": TRADE_DATE, "start_date": "2026-01-02",
        "end_date": TRADE_DATE, "indicator": "rsi", "topic": "Fed rate cut", "freq": "quarterly"}


class ScriptedModel(BaseChatModel):
    """Calls every bound tool once, then answers with TEXT."""

    structured: bool = False
    tools: tuple = ()
    calls: list = Field(default_factory=list)   # shared across bound copies
    threads: set = Field(default_factory=set)   # threads that served a tool-bound call
    fail_at: int | None = None                  # raise on this call, once

    @property
    def _llm_type(self) -> str:
        return "scripted"

    def bind_tools(self, tools, **kwargs):
        return self.model_copy(update={"tools": tuple(tools)})

    def with_structured_output(self, schema, **kwargs):
        if not self.structured:
            raise NotImplementedError
        return RunnableLambda(lambda _: self._count() or STRUCTURED[schema])

    def _count(self) -> None:
        self.calls.append(1)
        if len(self.calls) == self.fail_at:
            raise RuntimeError("provider unavailable")

    def _generate(self, messages, stop=None, run_manager=None, **kwargs) -> ChatResult:
        self._count()
        if self.tools:
            import threading
            import time
            self.threads.add(threading.current_thread().name)
            time.sleep(0.05)   # long enough for concurrent analysts to overlap
        if self.tools and not isinstance(messages[-1], ToolMessage):
            calls = [{"name": t.name, "id": f"call_{i}",
                      "args": {k: v for k, v in ARGS.items()
                               if k in t.tool_call_schema.model_json_schema()["properties"]}}
                     for i, t in enumerate(self.tools)]
            message = AIMessage(content="", tool_calls=calls)
        else:
            message = AIMessage(content=TEXT)
        return ChatResult(generations=[ChatGeneration(message=message)])

    def checkpoint_input(self, init_state):
        """The value to stream/invoke: ``None`` to resume an existing checkpoint,
        else the initial state for a fresh run.

        LangGraph resumes an interrupted thread when invoked with ``None``;
        re-passing the initial state instead appends it through the message
        reducer, duplicating messages in the resumed state (#1249).

        return None if self._resuming else init_state

        if self._checkpointer_ctx is not None:

    def load_entries(self) -> list[dict]:
        """Parse all entries from log. Returns list of dicts."""
        if not self._log_path or not self._log_path.exists():
            return []
        text = self._log_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        raw_entries = [e.strip() for e in text.split(self._SEPARATOR) if e.strip()]
        entries = []
        for raw in raw_entries:
            parsed = self._parse_entry(raw)
            if parsed:
                entries.append(parsed)
        return entries

    def get_pending_entries(self) -> list[dict]:
        """Return entries with outcome:pending, for settlement."""
        return [e for e in self.load_entries() if e.get("pending")]

    CIT-T6 calls this out separately; here it guards the numbering routine.

    from tradingagents.agents.citations import build_report_paragraphs

    paragraphs = build_report_paragraphs(
        {"market_report": "", "sentiment_report": "Sentiment only.",
         "news_report": "", "fundamentals_report": FUNDAMENTALS, "options_report": ""}
    )

    sources = {p["source"] for p in paragraphs}
    assert sources == {"SEN", "FUN"}
    assert ids_for_sources(paragraphs, "MKT") == []
    assert ids_for_sources(paragraphs, "FUN") == ["FUN-01", "FUN-02"]


def ids_for_sources(paragraphs, source):
    return [p["id"] for p in paragraphs if p["source"] == source]

    appends each notice to its own argument only."""

    argument-level citations into the debate state."""

def test_cit_t3_a_first_reply_may_reuse_the_same_paragraph_and_progress():
    """CIT-T3 / FR-DEB-01+FR-CIT-01: the bear's first reply using the bull's
    ID resolves to that paragraph, and a PROGRESS judgement continues the debate."""
    from tradingagents.agents.citations import resolve_turn

    from tradingagents.agents.researchers.bear_researcher import create_bear_researcher

    paragraphs = report_map()
    bull_turn = "Bull Analyst: Revenue grew 10% [FUN-01]."
    bear_turn = "Bear Analyst: That 10% came from one customer [FUN-01], which is concentration risk."

    bull_entry = resolve_turn("bull", 2, bull_turn, paragraphs)
    bear_entry = resolve_turn("bear", 2, "That 10% came from one customer [FUN-01], which is concentration risk.", paragraphs)
    assert citations_of(bull_entry["arguments"][0]) == ["FUN-01"]
    assert citations_of(bear_entry["arguments"][0]) == ["FUN-01"]

    judgement = MagicMock()
    judgement.outcome = PROGRESS
    node = create_bear_researcher(RecordingLLM(bear_turn), judge=_scripted_judge(judgement))
    state = _state(paragraphs, debate={

        "bear_history": "\nBear Analyst: earlier.",
        "current_response": bull_turn, "count": 3,
    })

    assert debate["progress_reason"] == ""
    assert "FUN-01" in debate["history"]


def _scripted_judge(result):
    class _Judge:
        def invoke(self, prompt):
            return result

    return _Judge()

# --- CIT-T3 · fit criterion: no misplaced or ambiguous citation -----------


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_cit_t3_a_valid_id_is_never_also_reported_invalid():
    """Fit criterion 'wrongly flagged citation': a written, resolvable ID carries
    exactly one verdict and no notice."""
    from tradingagents.agents.citations import resolve_turn

    entry = resolve_turn("bull", 1, "Demand is intact [FUN-01] and margins held [FUN-02].",
                         report_map())
    claims = [c for a in entry["arguments"] for c in a["citations"]]
    assert [c["id"] for c in claims] == ["FUN-01", "FUN-02"]
    assert all(c["valid"] for c in claims)
    assert [a["note"] for a in entry["arguments"]] == [""]


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_cit_t3_an_id_from_another_report_is_never_rewritten():
    """Fit criterion 'misplaced citation': an ID that names another run paragraph
    is judged against the map as written — never interpreted as FUN-02."""
    from tradingagents.agents.citations import extract_citations

    positions = extract_citations("Margin fell [MKT-02] on the day.")
    assert [p["id"] for p in positions] == ["MKT-02"]
    assert positions[0]["position"] == len("Margin fell ")

@pytest.mark.unit
def test_cit_t9_the_graph_layout_is_unchanged():
    """CIT-T9 / AGENTS.md: editing the bull/bear/manager nodes adds no node,
    edge or route; the debate and risk routers keep their exact target maps."""
    import ast
    import inspect
    import textwrap

    from tradingagents.graph import setup as setup_module

    assert set(DEBATE_PATH_MAP) == {"Bull Researcher", "Bear Researcher", "Research Manager"}
    assert set(RISK_ANALYSIS_PATH_MAP) == {
        "Aggressive Analyst", "Conservative Analyst", "Neutral Analyst", "Portfolio Manager",
    }

    tree = ast.parse(textwrap.dedent(inspect.getsource(setup_module.GraphSetup.setup_graph)))

            if isinstance(c, ast.Call) and isinstance(c.func, ast.Attribute)}
    assert adds == {"add_node", "add_edge", "add_conditional_edges"}, adds

# --- judgement scheduling: call counts and boundary ------------------------


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_judgement_is_scheduled_only_for_complete_rounds_between_two_and_cap():
    """FR-DEB-01: judged only when 2 <= round < cap, i.e. even count with
    4 <= count < 2*cap. At most max(0, cap-2) evaluations per run."""
    from tradingagents.graph.setup import GraphSetup  # noqa: F401  (wiring present)

    # The scheduler lives in the bear node; the contract is expressed here as the
    # set of counts that must be judged, independent of the implementation.
    def judged(count, cap):
        return count % 2 == 0 and 4 <= count < 2 * cap

    assert [c for c in range(0, 9) if judged(c, 1)] == []
    assert [c for c in range(0, 9) if judged(c, 2)] == []
    assert [c for c in range(0, 9) if judged(c, 3)] == [4]
    assert [c for c in range(0, 11) if judged(c, 4)] == [4, 6]
    assert max(0, 3 - 2) == 1 and max(0, 2 - 2) == 0 and max(0, 4 - 2) == 2

"""Shared pytest fixtures that prevent CI hangs when API keys are absent."""

import os
import socket

import pytest


def _blank_settings_overlay():
    """Blank every TRADINGAGENTS_* setting before the package is imported.

    The package loads .env on import and folds these variables into
    DEFAULT_CONFIG, so a contributor's own settings would become the defaults
    the suite asserts on. A blank value is still present, so load_dotenv leaves
    it alone, and the overlay reads it as unset. Tests of the overlay set their own.
    """
    from dotenv import dotenv_values, find_dotenv

    names = set(os.environ)
    for filename in (".env", ".env.enterprise"):
        names |= set(dotenv_values(find_dotenv(filename, usecwd=True)))
    for name in names:
        if name.startswith("TRADINGAGENTS_"):
            os.environ[name] = ""


_blank_settings_overlay()


def _own_file_locations():
    """Keep the suite's results, cache and memory log in a directory of its own.

    Set before the package is imported, whose defaults put them in the user's
    home: a test reading the user's cache would see what their runs fetched.
    """
    import tempfile

    home = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="tradingagents-tests-")
    os.environ["TRADINGAGENTS_RESULTS_DIR"] = os.path.join(home, "logs")
    os.environ["TRADINGAGENTS_CACHE_DIR"] = os.path.join(home, "cache")
    os.environ["TRADINGAGENTS_MEMORY_LOG_PATH"] = os.path.join(home, "memory", "trading_memory.md")


_own_file_locations()


def pytest_configure(config):
    for marker in ("unit", "integration", "smoke"):
        config.addinivalue_line("markers", f"{marker}: {marker}-level tests")
    # yfinance caches each symbol's time zone on disk, in the home directory
    # by default; the suite keeps it in a directory of its own.
    import tempfile

    import yfinance

    yfinance.set_tz_cache_location(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="tradingagents-tests-yf-"))

def _company_background_markdown(view: dict) -> str:
    """The Company Background section for a prepared profile view.

    One field per line, missing fields omitted. A historical run's view carries
    only a name, shown as today's. An empty view shows the unavailable notice.
    Field values come from the raw shared view and are Markdown-escaped here so
    the reader sees the source text literally, matching the HTML report.
    """
    lines = []
    if view.get("name"):
        suffix = " (current name)" if view["name_is_current"] else ""
        lines.append(f"- Name: {_md_escape(view['name'])}{suffix}")
    if view.get("industry"):
        lines.append(f"- Industry: {_md_escape(view['industry'])}")
    if view.get("business_description"):
        lines.append(f"- Business: {_md_escape(view['business_description'])}")
    body = "\n".join(lines) if lines else BACKGROUND_UNAVAILABLE
    return f"## Company Background\n\n{body}"


def analyst_names(keys) -> list[str]:
    """The analysts as users select them: the sentiment analyst's key is "social"."""
    return ["sentiment" if key == "social" else key for key in keys or []]


def _header(ticker: str, final_state: dict, settings: dict | None) -> str:

    entry = resolve_turn("bear", 1, turn, paragraphs)

    assert [citations_of(a) for a in entry["arguments"]] == [[]]
    assert entry["arguments"][0]["note"] == UNCITED


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_cit_t8_a_label_stays_in_the_argument_that_wrote_it():
    """CIT-T8: a label from one argument (or another turn) is not attributed to
    the current one, and its inline position is preserved."""
    from tradingagents.agents.citations import resolve_turn

    turn = "Margins fell [FUN-01].\n\nVolume rose."
    entry = resolve_turn("bear", 2, turn, report_map())

    first, second = entry["arguments"]
    assert citations_of(first) == ["FUN-01"]
    assert first["citations"][0]["position"] == first["text"].index("[FUN-01]")
    assert second["citations"] == []
    assert second["note"] == UNCITED


@pytest.mark.unit

    """The reports a run supplies, keyed by state field (the ``build_*`` input).

    ``exclude`` leaves an analyst unselected (its report is empty); ``overrides``
    replaces a report's text with ``<name>=`` (bare or with the ``_report``
    suffix). This is the one source of report text: the state and the expected
    paragraph map are both derived from it, so they cannot disagree.
    """
    texts = {key: f"Report for {key}." for key in PREFIX}
    for name, value in overrides.items():
        texts[_resolve(name)] = value
    for name in exclude:
        texts[_resolve(name)] = ""
    return texts


# The blueprint's source words, accepted alongside the state field names.
_SOURCE_NAME = {
    "market": "market_report", "sentiment": "sentiment_report",
    "news": "news_report", "fundamental": "fundamentals_report",
    "option": "options_report",
}


def _resolve(name):
    """The report state field for ``name`` (``fundamentals`` or ``fundamentals_report``)."""
    key = name if name.endswith("_report") else f"{name}_report"

def _source_paragraphs(text):
    paragraphs = []
    for block in re.split(r"\n[ \t]*\n", text or ""):
        if not block.strip():
            continue
        lines = [line.strip() for line in block.splitlines() if line.strip()]
        if len(lines) == 1 and HEADING.fullmatch(lines[0]):
            continue
        if lines and HEADING.fullmatch(lines[0]) and len(lines) > 1:
            test_first = lines[0][1:].strip()
            if test_first and lines[1].startswith(test_first):
                lines = lines[1:]
        paragraphs.append("\n".join(lines))
    return paragraphs

def _markdown() -> MarkdownIt:
    md = MarkdownIt("commonmark", {"html": False}).enable("table").disable("image")
    md.add_render_rule("table_open", lambda *a: '<div class="table"><table>\n')
    md.add_render_rule("table_close", lambda *a: "</table></div>\n")
    return md


def _render_agent_text(md: MarkdownIt, text: str) -> str:
    """An agent's text, its own headings placed below the agent's heading (h3)."""
    tokens = md.parse(text)
    for token in tokens:
        if token.type in ("heading_open", "heading_close"):
            token.tag = f"h{min(int(token.tag[1]) + 3, 6)}"
    return md.renderer.render(tokens, md.options, {})

    "news_data": "News", "macro_data": "Macro", "prediction_markets": "Prediction markets",
    "options_data": "Options",
}


def _fields(values) -> str:
    return " ".join(f'<span class="field">{escape(str(v))}</span>' for v in values)

    def checkpoint_input(self, init_state):
        """The value to stream/invoke: ``None`` to resume an existing checkpoint,
        else the initial state for a fresh run.

        LangGraph resumes an interrupted thread when invoked with ``None``;
        re-passing the initial state instead appends it through the message
        reducer, duplicating messages in the resumed state (#1249).
        """

    def load_entries(self) -> list[dict]:
        """Parse all entries from log. Returns list of dicts."""
        if not self._log_path or not self._log_path.exists():
            return []
        text = self._log_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        raw_entries = [e.strip() for e in text.split(self._SEPARATOR) if e.strip()]
        entries = []
        for raw in raw_entries:
            parsed = self._parse_entry(raw)
            if parsed:
                entries.append(parsed)
        return entries

    def get_pending_entries(self) -> list[dict]:
        """Return entries with outcome:pending, for settlement."""
        return [e for e in self.load_entries() if e.get("pending")]

@pytest.mark.unit
def test_cit_t1_both_researchers_see_the_same_labels_on_the_original_paragraphs():
    """CIT-T1 / FR-CIT-01: the labels are on the same original text for bull and
    bear, the heading has no ID, and the options report starts at OPT-01."""
    from tradingagents.agents.researchers.bear_researcher import create_bear_researcher
    from tradingagents.agents.researchers.bull_researcher import create_bull_researcher

    paragraphs = report_map(options_report="## Chain\n\nCalls are bid at 1.2.\n\nSpreads widened.")
    state = _state(paragraphs)

    bull, bear = RecordingLLM(), RecordingLLM()
    create_bull_researcher(bull)(dict(state))
    create_bear_researcher(bear)(dict(state))

    said = "\n".join(_prompt_text(p) for p in bull.prompts + bear.prompts)
    assert f"[FUN-01] {FUN_01}" in said
    assert f"[FUN-02] {FUN_02}" in said
    assert "# Fundamentals" not in said or "[FUN-00]" not in said
    assert "[OPT-01]" in said and "Calls are bid at 1.2." in said
    assert "[FUN-01] # Fundamentals" not in said

    ids = [p["id"] for p in paragraphs if p["report_key"] == "options_report"]
    assert ids == ["OPT-01", "OPT-02"]
