def _markdown() -> MarkdownIt:
    md = MarkdownIt("commonmark", {"html": False}).enable("table").disable("image")
    md.add_render_rule("table_open", lambda *a: '<div class="table"><table>\n')
    md.add_render_rule("table_close", lambda *a: "</table></div>\n")
    return md


def _render_agent_text(md: MarkdownIt, text: str) -> str:
    """An agent's text, its own headings placed below the agent's heading (h3)."""
    tokens = md.parse(text)
    for token in tokens:
        if token.type in ("heading_open", "heading_close"):
            token.tag = f"h{min(int(token.tag[1]) + 3, 6)}"
    return md.renderer.render(tokens, md.options, {})

It depends on the citation leaf only.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom tradingagents.agents.citations import (\n    build_report_paragraphs,\n    render_history_turn,\n    render_numbered_reports,\n    resolve_turn,\n)\nfrom tradingagents.agents.context import report_or_absent\n\nREPORT_SOURCES = (\n    (\"market_report\", \"market\"),\n    (\"sentiment_report\", \"sentiment\"),\n    (\"news_report\", \"news\"),\n    (\"fundamentals_report\", \"fundamentals\"),\n    (\"options_report\", \"options\"),\n)\n\n\ndef reports_for(state) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"The five supplied reports, keyed by state field.\"\"\"\n    return {key: state.get(key, \"\") for key, _source in REPORT_SOURCES}\n\n\ndef debate_report_paragraphs(state) -> list:\n    \"\"\"This run's numbered paragraphs: the stored map, or one built once.\n\n    A run builds the map before its first researcher's model call, and every\n    later turn reuses the map from the state \u2014 including a present empty map.\n    \"\"\"\n    paragraphs = state[\"investment_debate_state\"].get(\"report_paragraphs\")\n    if paragraphs is None:\n        paragraphs = build_report_paragraphs(reports_for(state))\n    return paragraphs\n\n\ndef numbered_reports(state, paragraphs) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"The reports as the researchers read them: ``[ID] paragraph`` each.\n\n    A report with no numbered paragraph keeps its own text, so a deselected\n    analyst still reads as absent rather than as an empty finding.\n    \"\"\"\n    return render_numbered_reports(reports_for(state), paragraphs)\n\n\ndef prompt_report(reports, key, source) -> str:\n    \"\"\"One report as it goes into a researcher's prompt.\"\"\"\n    return report_or_absent(reports[key], source)\n\n\ndef record_turn(state, speaker: str, text: str, paragraphs) -> tuple[str, dict]:\n    \"\"\"Annotate one model turn and return ``(recorded_history_text, record)``.\n\n    The record keeps the model's own ``raw`` text; def write_report_tree(final_state: dict, ticker: str, save_path, settings: dict | None = None,
                      html: bool = True) -> Path:
    """Save a completed run's reports to ``save_path``; return the complete-report path.

    ``settings`` (``TradingAgentsGraph.run_settings()``) adds what produced the run
    to the report's header. ``html`` also writes ``complete_report.html``, one
    self-contained page of the same report (#1419).
    Reusing a directory replaces the generated report files, removing sections
    absent from this run and disabled HTML. Other files and directories are kept.
    """
    save_path = Path(save_path)
    save_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    parts = _report_parts(final_state)
    # Prepared once per export and shared by both formats (FEAT-03).
    background = build_company_background(final_state)
    background_md = _company_background_markdown(background) + "\n\n"
    sections = []
    for heading, folder, written in parts:
        (save_path / folder).mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        for _agent, filename, text in written:
            (save_path / folder / filename).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        content = "\n\n".join(f"### {agent}\n{text}" for agent, _filename, text in written)
        sections.append(f"## {heading}\n\n{content}")

    (save_path / "complete_report.md").write_text(
        _header(ticker, final_state, settings) + background_md + "\n\n".join(sections),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    if html:
        from tradingagents.report_html import render_report

        (save_path / "complete_report.html").write_text(
            render_report(ticker, final_state, settings, parts, background=background),
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
    else:
        (save_path / "complete_report.html").unlink(missing_ok=True)

    # Reconcile only the filenames owned by this writer; never clear the tree,
    # since callers may keep notes or other artifacts alongside the reports.
    current_files = {
        (folder, filename)
        for _heading, folder, written in parts
        for _agent, filename, _text in written
    }
    for _heading, folder, agents in _SECTIONS:
        for _agent, filename, _path in agents:
            if (folder, filename) not in current_files:
                (save_path / folder / filename).unlink(missing_ok=True)
    return save_path / "complete_report.md"

```

```markdown
The trailing `---` is part of the preceding block's text. If I put the rule as a *leading* line spaced away, the block helper would create a standalone `---` block. Instead, use an HTML comment-free structural separator that Markdown treats as a paragraph break without appearing as a block: adjacent paragraphs in Markdown only merge when they are plain text. A **blank-line-separated list item** does render separately, so the marker approach is what works — and the test accepts blocks beginning with a marker only if the *label* is stripped first. The label must therefore precede the marker on the same line, which is `Bear Analyst: + text`, and the test strips `Bear Analyst: ` leaving `+ text` — not equal. So the marker cannot be there.

The clean solution: the recorded history text itself must contain the approved structure — one paragraph per argument (already true) — and the *Markdown renderer* must be told not to merge paragraphs. CommonMark merges plain paragraphs only when they are adjacent lines; blank-separated paragraphs render as separate `<p>` always. Let me verify that directly.

"""FEAT-05 / FR-CIT-01: trace bull and bear arguments to numbered paragraphs.

The analysts' reports are numbered once per run, before the debate starts. Each
numbered paragraph is then shown to the researchers as ``[PREFIX-NN] text``, and
every argument a researcher writes is resolved against that same map: a written
ID is valid when this run's map holds it, and every argument carries either no
notice (its IDs all resolve), ``Invalid citation`` (an ID the map does not hold)
or ``No citation provided`` (no ID at all).

The annotations are derived from the model's text, never written into it. A
turn's record keeps ``raw`` exactly as the model wrote it and ``arguments`` as
the resolved pieces, so re-rendering a recorded turn — a resume, a re-export —
yields the same annotated text once, notices included.

This module is a leaf: it imports nothing from the rest of the package, so the
analyst and report layers never depend on the debate contract.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

# Stable display wording (approved). A notice trails its own argument.
INVALID = "Invalid citation"
UNCITED = "No citation provided"

# One prefix per supplied report, in the order the analysts are numbered.
REPORT_PREFIXES = (
    ("market_report", "MKT"),
    ("sentiment_report", "SEN"),
    ("news_report", "NWS"),
    ("fundamentals_report", "FUN"),
    ("options_report", "OPT"),
)

_SPEAKER = {"bull": "Bull Analyst", "bear": "Bear Analyst"}

# A written citation label: three letters, a hyphen, two digits.
_LABEL = re.compile(r"\[([A-Z]{3}-[0-9]{2})\]")
# A list item's opening marker, replaced so a rendered turn keeps one marker.
_LIST_PREFIX = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:[-*+]|\d+[.)])\s+")
# The same marker, matched only at a block's own start (never across a newline).
_LEADING_MARKER = re.compile(r"^[ \t]*(?:[-*+]|\d+[.)])[ \t]+")
_HEADING = re.compile(r"#{1,6}\s.*")
_FENCE = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:```|~~~)")
# A list item opening a line: a bullet or an ordered marker.
_LIST_ITEM = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:[-*+]|\d+[.)])\s+")


@dataclass
class Argument:
    """One resolved argument of a debate turn."""

    text: str
    citations: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
    note: str = ""


# --- numbering the supplied reports ---------------------------------------

def build_report_paragraphs(reports: Mapping[str, str]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Number every supplied report's paragraphs, in analyst order.

    Each non-empty report is numbered from ``01`` under its own prefix, so a map
    never depends on which other analysts ran. The result is a list of
    ``{"id", "source", "report_key", "text"}`` dicts.
    """
    paragraphs: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for key, prefix in REPORT_PREFIXES:
        for n, text in enumerate(_source_paragraphs(reports.get(key, "")), 1):
            paragraphs.append({
                "id": f"{prefix}-{n:02d}",
                "source": prefix,
                "report_key": key,
                "text": text,
            })
    return paragraphs


def _source_paragraphs(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """A report's paragraphs: blank-line blocks, headings given no ID.

    Source segmentation differs from argument segmentation: a block of adjacent
    list items is ONE paragraph here (it was written as one passage), whereas a
    debate turn splits each list item into its own argument. A block that is only
    headings is skipped; a one-line heading directly above body text contributes
    the body.
    """
    paragraphs = []
    for block in re.split(r"\n[ \t]*\n", text or ""):
        lines = [line for line in block.splitlines() if line.strip()]
        if not lines:
            continue
        if _HEADING.fullmatch(lines[0].strip()):
            if len(lines) == 1:
                continue  # a heading on its own gets no ID
            lines = lines[1:]  # a one-line heading directly above body text
        if all(_HEADING.fullmatch(line.strip()) for line in lines):
            continue
        paragraphs.append("\n".join(lines))
    return paragraphs


def render_numbered_reports(reports: Mapping[str, str], paragraphs: Iterable[dict]) -> str:
    """The reports as the researchers read them: one labelled paragraph each.

    Reports with no numbered paragraph are returned unchanged, so a deselected
    analyst still reads as its own ``report_or_absent`` marker.
    """
    by_key: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for paragraph in paragraphs:
        by_key.setdefault(paragraph["report_key"], []).append(
            f"[{paragraph['id']}] {paragraph['text']}")
    rendered = {}
    for key, _prefix in REPORT_PREFIXES:
        labelled = by_key.get(key)
        rendered[key] = "\n\n".join(labelled) if labelled else (reports.get(key) or "")
    return rendered


# --- segmenting a debate turn ---------------------------------------------

def split_arguments(turn: str) -> list[Argument]:
    """Split a model's turn into arguments, each able to carry its own notice.

    An argument is a blank-line block, where:
      - each list item (with its indented continuation) is its own argument;
      - a fenced block is not an argument: it attaches in full to the argument
        before it, or stands alone when it leads the turn;
      - a table's rows are one argument.
    """
    arguments: list[str] = []
    for block in re.split(r"\n[ \t]*\n", turn or ""):
        if not block.strip():
            continue
        current: list[str] = []
        fenced = False
        for line in block.splitlines():
            if _FENCE.match(line):
                fenced = not fenced
                current.append(line)
                continue
            if fenced or not _LIST_ITEM.match(line):
                current.append(line)
                continue

            # a leading fenced b

`TradingAgentsGraph.propagate(...)` → the compiled graph's `Bull Researcher` node. def report_map(exclude=(), **overrides):
    """The expected map for a run supplying ``report_texts(exclude, ...)``.

    An independent restatement of the approved numbering, so a wrong
    implementation of ``build_report_paragraphs`` cannot pass by agreeing with
    itself.
    """
    return expected_map(report_texts(exclude, **overrides))


def _source_paragraphs(text):
    """An independent restatement of the approved source segmentation.

    Blank-line blocks; a block that is only headings is skipped; a block whose
    first line is a one-line heading followed by body text contributes the body.
    """
    paragraphs = []
    for block in re.split(r"\n[ \t]*\n", text or ""):
        lines = [line for line in block.splitlines() if line.strip()]
        if not lines:
            continue
        if re.fullmatch(r"#{1,6}\s.*", lines[0].strip()):
            if len(lines) == 1:
                continue  # a heading on its own gets no ID
            lines = lines[1:]  # one-line heading directly above body text
        body = "\n".join(lines)
        if body.strip() and not all(re.fullmatch(r"#{1,6}\s.*", line.strip()) for line in lines):
            paragraphs.append(body)
    return paragraphs

def html_blocks(fragment):
    """The text of each block-level element in ``fragment``, tags stripped."""
    blocks = re.findall(r"<(p|li|td|th|h[1-6])[^>]*>(.*?)</\1>", fragment, flags=re.S)
    return [(tag, unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", body)).strip()) for tag, body in blocks]

def _markdown() -> MarkdownIt:
    md = MarkdownIt("commonmark", {"html": False}).enable("table").disable("image")
    md.add_render_rule("table_open", lambda *a: '<div class="table"><table>\n')
    md.add_render_rule("table_close", lambda *a: "</table></div>\n")
    return md


def _render_agent_text(md: MarkdownIt, text: str) -> str:
    """An agent's text, its own headings placed below the agent's heading (h3)."""
    tokens = md.parse(text)
    for token in tokens:
        if token.type in ("heading_open", "heading_close"):
            token.tag = f"h{min(int(token.tag[1]) + 3, 6)}"
    return md.renderer.render(tokens, md.options, {})

[Tool result]: def write_report_tree(final_state: dict, ticker: str, save_path, settings: dict | None = None,
                      html: bool = True) -> Path:
    """Save a completed run's reports to ``save_path``; return the complete-report path.

    ``settings`` (``TradingAgentsGraph.run_settings()``) adds what produced the run
    to the report's header. ``html`` also writes ``complete_report.html``, one
    self-contained page of the same report (#1419).
    Reusing a directory replaces the generated report files, removing sections
    absent from this run and disabled HTML. Other files and directories are kept.
    """
    save_path = Path(save_path)
    save_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    parts = _report_parts(final_state)
    # Prepared once per export and shared by both formats (FEAT-03).
    background = build_company_background(final_state)
    background_md = _company_background_markdown(background) + "\n\n"
    sections = []
    for heading, folder, written in parts:
        (save_path / folder).mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        for _agent, filename, text in written:
            (save_path / folder / filename).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        content = "\n\n".join(f"### {agent}\n{text}" for agent, _filename, text in written)
        sections.append(f"## {heading}\n\n{content}")

    (save_path / "complete_report.md").write_text(
        _header(ticker, final_state, settings) + background_md + "\n\n".join(sections),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    if html:
        from tradingagents.report_html import render_report

        (save_path / "complete_report.html").write_text(
            render_report(ticker, final_state, settings, parts, background=background),
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
    else:
        (save_path / "complete_report.html").unlink(missing_ok=True)

    # Reconcile only the filenames owned by this writer; never clear the tree,
    # since callers may keep notes or other artifacts alongside the reports.
    current_files

def assert_arguments_rendered(blocks, expected=EXPECTED_BEAR):
    """Each approved argument sits verbatim in exactly one block.

    Called on a fragment holding only the recorded turns: the speaker's own
    label (``Bear Analyst:``) prefixes the first block of its turn.
    """
    joined = [block.removeprefix("Bear Analyst: ").removeprefix("Bull Analyst: ")
              for block in blocks]

"""FEAT-05: the numbered reports a researcher reads and the absent-report marker.

Only the label rendering lives here; the citation leaf itself is imported by
each researcher directly, so both nodes depend on it explicitly.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

    ("market_report", "market"),

    ("news_report", "news"),
    ("fundamentals_report", "fundamentals"),
    ("options_report", "options"),
)


def reports_for(state) -> dict:
    """The five supplied reports, keyed by state field."""
    return {key: state.get(key, "") for key, _source in REPORT_SOURCES}

The full diff is in the review pane; the substance:

- **`agents/citations.py` (new, leaf)** — imports nothing from the package. `build_report_paragraphs` numbers each supplied report from `01` under `MKT/SEN/NWS/FUN/OPT` (headings get no ID; source blocks follow blank lines, so adjacent list items share one ID). `split_arguments` segments a turn (each list item separate, fenced blocks attach to the preceding argument, a table is one argument). `extract_citations`, `resolve_turn` (record `{speaker, turn, raw, arguments}` with positions, validity, one notice per argument), `render_annotated_turn` (derived from the record, so re-render cannot duplicate a notice), plus `render_for_prompt` / `render_numbered_report` and `render_for_reader`.
- **bull/bear researchers** — import the leaf directly; read `report_paragraphs` from state and build it only when absent (a present map, including `{}`, is reused verbatim); show labelled reports in the prompt; append `report_paragraphs` and the turn's record to `turn_citations`.
- **research_manager** — carries `report_paragraphs`/`turn_citations` through without importing the leaf.
- **state.py / trading_graph.py** — two optional annotations and two additive run-log keys; existing keys keep their values.
- **reporting.py** — analyst reports labelled with their IDs; recorded turns passed through unchanged; a blank line after each agent heading so a turn's first line starts its own block.

Preserved: graph nodes, edges, routes, router logic, public factory signatures, CLI defaults, `_run_signal`/run signature, and the pre-existing `opencode.json` and `docs/ai-use-log.yaml` changes.

## 2. How the normal entry point reaches the feature

`TradingAgentsGraph.propagate(...)` → the compiled graph's `Bull Researcher` node. On its first call `investment_debate_state` has no `report_paragraphs` (the initial state deliberately omits it), so `build_report_paragraphs` numbers the analyst reports before the model is called and the node stores the map. The bear reuses that stored map. Both append their record to `turn_citations`.

Verified end-to-end on the offline scripted model through `propagate` + `save_reports`:

@pytest.mark.unit
def test_reg_a_debate_fence_under_a_claim_takes_the_claims_notice():
    """Finding 3: attachment decides the notice. The claim's citation governs
    the whole argument, so no uncited notice is raised for the fence."""
    from tradingagents.agents.citations import render_annotated_turn, resolve_turn

    turn = "Claim [FUN-01].\n\n```\nx=1\n```"
    entry = resolve_turn("bear", 1, turn, _paragraphs("First fact."))

    assert len(entry["arguments"]) == 1, entry["arguments"]
    argument = entry["arguments"][0]
    assert [c["id"] for c in argument["citations"]] == ["FUN-01"]
    assert argument["citations"][0]["valid"] is False  # FUN-01 is not in this tiny map
    assert argument["note"] == INVALID, "the claim's own citation governs the argument"

    rendered = render_annotated_turn(entry)
    assert UNCITED not in rendered, "the fence must not take its own notice"
    assert "x=1" in rendered


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_reg_a_debate_fence_still_attaches_after_a_blank_line_between():
    """Finding 3 contrast: the same turn with the fence separated by a blank
    line still attaches, so the two shapes agree."""
    turn = "Claim [FUN-01].\n\n```\nx=1\n```"
    assert split_arguments(turn) == split_arguments("Claim [FUN-01].\n```\nx=1\n```")

def notice_suffix(argument: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str:
    """The text appended to an argument for its notice, or ``""`` for none."""
    note = argument.get("note") or ""
    if not note:
        return ""
    if note == INVALID:
        written = ", ".join(
            claim["id"] for claim in argument.get("citations", ()) if not claim["valid"])
        return f" — *{INVALID}: {written}.*"
    return f" — *{note}.*"


def render_annotated_turn(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str:
    """The recorded turn as text: one argument per paragraph, notices in place.

    Derived from the stored records, never from text that already carries a
    notice, so rendering the same record twice cannot duplicate one.
    """
    rendered = [argument["text"] + notice_suffix(argument)
                for argument in entry.get("arguments", ())]
    if not rendered:
        return entry.get("raw", "")
    return "\n\n".join(rendered)


def reports_from_state(state) -> dict:
    """The five supplied reports from a run's state, keyed by state field."""
    return {key: state.get(key, "") for key, _prefix in REPORT_PREFIXES}


def render_numbered_report(report_key: str, text: str, paragraphs) -> str:
    """A report as the researchers read it: one ``[ID] paragraph`` per paragraph.

    Headings and fenced code keep their place in the report, whole and
    unnumbered, so the model reads the same report it would have read without
    labels and no body is duplicated. A report with no numbered paragraph is
    returned unchanged, so a deselected analyst still reads as absent rather
    than as an empty finding.
    """
    numbered = iter(p for p in paragraphs or () if p.get("report_key") == report_key)
    rendered = []

def _arguments_of_turn(turn):
    """The arguments of one recorded turn, with the speaker label removed.

    The label belongs to the turn, not to its first argument, so removing it
    lets that first argument be validated like every other one.
    """
    body = re.sub(r"^(?:Bull|Bear) Analyst: ", "", turn)
    return [a for a in re.split(r"\n[ \t]*\n", body) if a.strip()]


def citation_ids(argument):
    """The IDs an argument cites, as written.

    An ID that appears inside a notice is the notice's own subject, not a
    citation the argument makes, so it is not counted.
    """
    claims = argument
    for notice in (INVALID, UNCITED):
        claims = re.sub(re.escape(notice) + r":?[^.*]*", "", claims)
    return re.findall(r"\[([A-Z]{3}-[0-9]{2})\]", claims)


def assert_notice_once_per_argument(history):

    """The text appended to an argument for its notice, or ``""`` for none.

    An argument whose own words already end with its notice keeps that notice
    and gets no second one, so a speaker that echoes the phrase is annotated

    and the stored ``note`` and ``citations`` are untouched.

    note = argument.get("note") or ""

        return ""

    if note == INVALID:
        if re.search(rf"\*{INVALID}: [^*]*\*\s*\.?$", written):

        ids = ", ".join(
            claim["id"] for claim in argument.get("citations", ()) if not claim["valid"])

    if re.search(rf"\*{note}\*\s*\.?$", written):

    return f" — *{note}.*"

def notice_suffix(argument: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str:
    """The text appended to an argument for its notice, or ``""`` for none.

    An argument whose own words already end with its notice keeps that notice
    and gets no second one, so a speaker that echoes the phrase is annotated
    once. Only the suffix is suppressed: the model's text is never rewritten,
    and the stored ``note`` and ``citations`` are untouched.
    """
    note = argument.get("note") or ""
    if not note:
        return ""
    written = argument["text"].rstrip()
    if note == INVALID:
        if re.search(rf"\*{INVALID}: [^*]*\.?\*$", written):
            return ""
        ids = ", ".join(
            claim["id"] for claim in argument.get("citations", ()) if not claim["valid"])
        return f" — *{INVALID}: {ids}.*"
    if re.search(rf"\*{note}\.?\*$", written):
        return ""
    return f" — *{note}.*"



```
